content.title: Contraindications to fibrinolysis — table of agents, regimens and contraindications
content.notes: Table lists fibrinolytic molecules (rtPA, Streptokinase, Urokinase) with typical regimens and absolute/relative contraindications to fibrinolysis as shown on the page.

Absolute: History of haemorrhagic stroke or stroke of unknown origin
Major trauma, surgery, or head injury in previous 3 weeks
Relative: Transient ischaemic attack in previous 6 months

Regimen: 250,000 IU as a loading dose over 30 min, followed by 100,000 IU/h over 12–24 h
Accelerated regimen: 1.5 million IU over 2 h

Absolute: History of haemorrhagic stroke or stroke of unknown origin
Major trauma, surgery, or head injury in previous 3 weeks
Relative: Transient ischaemic attack in previous 6 months

Regimen: 4400 IU/kg as a loading dose over 10 min, followed by 4400 IU/kg/h over 12–24 h
Accelerated regimen: 3 million IU over 2 h

Absolute: History of haemorrhagic stroke or stroke of unknown origin
Major trauma, surgery, or head injury in previous 3 weeks
Relative: Transient ischaemic attack in previous 6 months
